title: Start Here: Terminal, Git, Python & uv
subtitle: Create the repository, understand the project files, and learn the commands you will use throughout the course.
analogy: A repository is the workshop. Git records the plans, pyproject.toml lists the materials, uv.lock records the exact materials chosen, and .venv is your isolated workbench.
objectives: Create and navigate a Git repository from the terminal.
Use uv to select Python, manage dependencies, and run project tools.
Explain what belongs in Git and what stays on your machine.
Prepare the package structure used by every later chapter.
prerequisites: A terminal and code editor. Commands use Bash/zsh on macOS or Linux; Windows learners should use WSL2 with Docker’s WSL integration.
Install Git, Docker Engine with Compose v2 (or Docker Desktop), uv, and curl. Install AWS CLI v2 and Terraform 1.11+ before the cloud chapters; links below cover platform-specific installation.

lessons.title: The tools and the baseline
body: This course uses Python 3.13 as a supported learning baseline, not as a claim about the newest Python release. The app uses FastAPI with Pydantic 2, async Psycopg 3, TaskIQ Streams, PostgreSQL 17, and Redis-compatible Valkey in AWS. Ruff handles linting/formatting, pytest checks behavior, and uv manages Python plus dependencies.
Use a dedicated learning AWS account for cloud exercises. NAT gateways, ALBs, databases and running containers incur charges. Local chapters need no AWS account.

lessons.title: Understand paths before copying commands
body: `pwd` prints the working directory. `cd` changes it; `..` means its parent. A relative path like `app/main.py` is interpreted from your current directory. Run project commands from the repository root unless a command explicitly uses `terraform -chdir=infra`.
The repository you create is the backend project, separate from the course reader. Do not put a second application inside this website repository.

lessons.title: Why uv replaces the manual pip workflow
body: `uv add` changes project dependencies and resolves a lockfile. `uv sync` creates or updates `.venv`; `uv run` runs a command with that environment. You do not need to activate the environment or install dependencies into system Python.

Commit `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock` and `.python-version`. A teammate runs `uv sync --locked` to reproduce the resolution. `--locked` fails on a stale lock; `--frozen` skips that freshness check. They are not interchangeable.

lessons.title: A minimal Python mental model
body: A module is a `.py` file; a package is a directory such as `app/` with `__init__.py`. `from app.config import Settings` imports a name. A function accepts inputs and returns a result. Type hints describe expected values; they do not by themselves validate HTTP input.

Pydantic validates request data in the API. A dictionary maps keys to values, a list holds ordered items, and an exception reports a failed operation. Read indentation as program structure; use four spaces.

Try the standalone python_basics.py example below: it demonstrates a type alias, a function, a dictionary, a for loop, a list comprehension, an if condition and try/except before those ideas appear inside the web application.

lessons.title: A repeatable daily loop
body: Create a branch, edit one behavior, run formatting/lint/tests, inspect `git diff`, then commit. The course will show complete file contents followed by explanations. A green unit test does not prove a database migration or cloud deployment works; later chapters add those checks.

handHoldingSteps: Install the prerequisites and verify their versions. If uv is missing, use its official installer or your package manager; restart the terminal so uv is on PATH.
Create `backend-bootcamp`, initialize Git, and initialize a bare uv project. Replace the generated pyproject.toml with the file shown below before resolving dependencies.
Create `app/`, `tests/`, `infra/` and `.github/workflows/`. Copy the ignore files and environment example. Create a short README explaining how to run the project.
Run `uv lock` and `uv sync --locked`. The first command resolves actual dependency versions; never hand-author uv.lock. Create application files in Chapter 2 before running its tests.

Inspect `git status` and `git diff --cached` before committing. `.env`, state and virtual environments must stay untracked. Create an empty remote repository in your Git hosting UI if you want to push.
concepts: Source vs environment: Python code and dependency declarations are shared; the installed `.venv` is machine-specific and recreated.
Lockfile vs manifest: pyproject.toml declares allowed versions; uv.lock stores the resolved graph. Review both when changing dependencies.
Environment variables: Local .env values are development examples. AWS injects production settings and database credentials at task startup.

commands.command:
# Optional, if uv is not installed on macOS/Linux:
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
# Restart the terminal, then verify:
uv --version
commands.explanation: Install uv using the official Astral installer, or follow the package-manager/platform alternatives linked below. The installer adds uv to your user tool directory.
commands.expected: uv is available on PATH; no global pip installation is needed.

commands.command:
git --version
uv --version
docker --version
docker compose version
curl --version
commands.explanation: Verify prerequisites before debugging application code. Install missing tools from the official links.
commands.expected: Each command prints a version; Compose must be v2.

commands.command:
mkdir backend-bootcamp
cd backend-bootcamp
git init -b main
uv init --bare --python 3.13
uv python install 3.13
uv python pin 3.13
mkdir -p app tests infra .github/workflows
touch app/__init__.py README.md
commands.explanation: Initialize the project. --bare skips a sample hello-world application; the app package will hold our API and worker.
commands.expected: A .git directory, pyproject.toml, .python-version, and the package folders exist.

commands.explanation: Practice inspecting folders without changing code.
commands.expected: You end in the repository root.

commands.command:
printf 'practice file\n' > notes.txt
cat notes.txt
cp notes.txt notes.backup.txt
mv notes.backup.txt notes.archive.txt
rm notes.archive.txt
commands.explanation: Practice creating, reading, copying, renaming and deleting one disposable file. rm has no undo; here it targets only the named practice copy.
commands.expected: notes.txt remains; the temporary archived copy is removed.

commands.command:
uv lock
uv sync --locked
uv run python --version
uv tree
commands.explanation: After copying pyproject.toml, resolve dependencies, install the locked environment and inspect the dependency tree.
Create local settings and verify they are ignored. This .env is for processes running on your host; Compose supplies its own container settings.

commands.command:
git add .gitignore .dockerignore .python-version .env.example pyproject.toml uv.lock app/__init__.py README.md
git diff --cached
git commit -m "Initialize uv backend project"
commands.explanation: Review and save the initial project, without committing credentials. Configure git user.name and user.email first if Git asks.
commands.expected: The first commit contains source/configuration only.

commands.command:
git switch -c feature/backend-api
git diff
git log --oneline -5
commands.explanation: Use a feature branch for Chapter 2 and learn how to inspect changes/history.

commands.command:
git remote add origin https://github.com/YOUR_OWNER/backend-bootcamp.git
git push -u origin main
commands.explanation: Optional: replace YOUR_OWNER and create the empty remote first. Authenticate with your Git host’s supported flow.
commands.expected: The main branch is published to your own repository.

commands.command:
uv add --dev pytest-cov
uv tree
uv remove --dev pytest-cov
git diff -- pyproject.toml uv.lock
commands.explanation: Optional dependency exercise: add a development-only test plugin, inspect the dependency graph, remove it, then review the manifest/lockfile changes. Use uv lock --upgrade-package PACKAGE for a deliberate package update, followed by tests.
commands.expected: The plugin is absent again; any remaining resolution changes are visible for review.

codeFiles.description: A small executable exercise before the framework code. Create examples/ first, then save and run this file with uv run --locked python examples/python_basics.py. It prints word counts, repeated words, and a handled validation error.

walkthrough.title: Types and functions
walkthrough.explanation: WordCounts names a dictionary type. The function accepts a string and returns a mapping. Type hints guide readers/tools; the explicit if/raise performs validation.

walkthrough.title: Loop and dictionary
walkthrough.explanation: casefold normalizes text, split produces a list, and the for loop updates dictionary counts. Indentation groups statements inside the loop.

walkthrough.title: Comprehension and exceptions
walkthrough.explanation: The list comprehension selects repeated words. try/except handles the expected ValueError from empty input without hiding unrelated failures.

walkthrough.title: Module entry point
walkthrough.explanation: The __name__ guard runs the exercise only when executing this file directly, not when another module imports count_words.

codeFiles.code:
[project]
name = "backend-bootcamp"
version = "0.1.0"
requires-python = ">=3.13,<3.14"
dependencies = [
  "fastapi>=0.115,<1",
  "uvicorn[standard]>=0.34,<1",
  "pydantic-settings>=2.7,<3",
  "psycopg[binary,pool]>=3.2,<4",
  "taskiq>=0.11,<1",
  "taskiq-redis>=1.0,<2",
]

[dependency-groups]
dev = ["ruff>=0.11,<1", "pytest>=8,<10", "httpx>=0.28,<1"]

[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py313"
line-length = 88

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["E", "F", "I", "UP", "B", "ASYNC"]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
pythonpath = ["."]
testpaths = ["tests"]
codeFiles.description: The project manifest. Copy this before running uv lock.

walkthrough.title: [project]
walkthrough.explanation: The Python range selects the 3.13 baseline; runtime dependencies are installed in containers.

walkthrough.title: [dependency-groups]
walkthrough.explanation: The dev group installs Ruff, pytest and HTTPX for local checks and CI. uv sync installs it by default; container builds use --no-dev.

walkthrough.title: [tool.ruff] and [tool.pytest]
walkthrough.explanation: Tools read their configuration here, so teammates and CI run the same checks.

breakItDrill.title: Detect a stale lockfile
breakItDrill.scenario: Change a dependency constraint in pyproject.toml, then run `uv sync --locked`.
breakItDrill.symptom: uv refuses to silently change the dependency resolution.
breakItDrill.fix: Run `uv lock`, review its diff, then sync again. Do not delete the lockfile just to silence the failure.

assignment.title: Document your setup
assignment.description: Write a README with installation prerequisites, repository structure, the Python baseline, and why uv.lock is committed. Create a feature branch for the next chapter.
assignment.completionHint: Verify the result yourself, then complete the chapter checklist.

recallNote.keyTakeaway: A reproducible project starts with explicit dependencies and a committed lockfile.
bullets: Use `uv run` instead of installing tools globally.
Use Bash/zsh or WSL consistently throughout the lab.
Git tracks source and lockfiles, never .env or Terraform state.

Use uv to select Python, manage dependencies, and run project tools.
